requestDefinition.note: Access-Control-Request-Headers carries header names only, not credentials.
requestDefinition.responseOutputFilter: Only status, exact requested origin / wildcard / absent / different-origin classification, POST/required-header booleans and the allowlisted ORIGIN_DENIED error are recorded. For a 403 body, one stream chunk is read and the stream is cancelled; only a chunk of at most 1024 bytes is parsed for error recognition. No raw response body is recorded.

interpretation.android: Confirmed rejected at the observed time: HTTP 403, no ACAO, fixed ORIGIN_DENIED. Advertised POST/header support alone does not make the preflight pass.
interpretation.existingWeb: Confirmed preflight acceptance for exactly https://genie-web-rosy.vercel.app and the three requested header names at the observed time.
interpretation.actionNeeded: Read the actual effective VS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configuration through an authorized private channel, preserve every existing entry and add exactly https://localhost. No configuration was changed by this task.
interpretation.sourceContext: The previously inspected deployed source returns an allowed OPTIONS at line 105 or origin rejection at line 104 before database client creation, Auth checks, quota RPC and provider invocation.

limits: No actual POST, signup, decision, sharing, voting, reporting, deletion or model call was performed.
A successful existing-web preflight does not establish a functioning web application, Auth settings, model availability or database behavior.
Only two origins and three requested header names were checked; no conclusion about all origins, additional SDK headers, WebView behavior or physical devices.
The exact VS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS environment value and whether the fallback list or an override produced the result remain unknown.
No keys, environment values, user rows, questions, votes, reports or raw request logs were read or persisted.
Platform access/monitoring logs may record these OPTIONS requests; no claim that every platform layer produced zero logs.
Results are a point-in-time observation and do not apply after a subsequent configuration or function change without new evidence.
